M., Uszkoreit, J., Le, Q., & Petrov, S. (2019). Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research. Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics.
creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov (Google Research)
description: A question answering dataset containing real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine, paired with Wikipedia pages and human annotations of long and short answers.
name: Natural Questions
rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 for training data, 5 for development and test data
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors conducted a post-hoc evaluation of annotation quality using consensus judgments from four experts on a subset of data, and analyzed variability using 25-way annotations on 302 examples to understand human agreement and ambiguity.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators complete three stages: 1) Question Identification (determine if the question is good/fact-seeking), 2) Long Answer Identification (select the earliest HTML bounding box containing enough information to infer the answer, or mark 'no answer'), 3) Short Answer Identification (select the entity/entities within the long answer that answer the question, or flag yes/no/no short answer).
rai:dataBiases: The authors acknowledge potential biases in choosing Wikipedia as the sole source of factual information, though they believe it is stylistically similar to other web sources.
rai:dataCollection: Questions are sampled from real queries of 8+ words issued to the Google search engine by multiple users. These are filtered using heuristics and run through Google search to keep those with a Wikipedia page in the top 5 results. Annotators then identify answers in the Wikipedia pages.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Annotators can mark 'no answer' (NULL) if the Wikipedia page does not answer the question or if the information is spread across many paragraphs. 51% of examples have no answer labeled.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine and Wikipedia pages from the top 5 search results.
rai:dataCollectionType: User-generated content data, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries are filtered using simple heuristics (e.g., starting with specific wh-words, containing multiple entities) to discard non-questions. Part of speech tags and entities are identified using Google's Cloud NLP API.
rai:dataUseCases: Open-domain question answering (QA) and natural language understanding (NLU) research.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Google's Cloud NLP API (used to identify part of speech tags and entities for query filtering heuristics)
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset uses real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine.

null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper mentions a pool of around 50 annotators but provides no demographic details.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No data imputation protocol is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No data manipulation or augmentation protocol is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No maintenance or update plan is described.
null_reasons.rai:dataSocialImpact: No specific discussion of social impact beyond general utility for NLU research.
null_reasons.rai:dataLimitations: No specific limitations of the dataset are discussed, other than the acknowledged bias of using Wikipedia.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The paper does not specify the timeframe during which the Google search queries were collected.
